method: Direct sequential reading of final current main, before comparison to author coverage inventory; custom source-derived observations, not yet protocol-normalized.

observations.statement: Mixed precision retains one order-forty denominator and shortens only one alternate numerator. Integral formal-group and logarithm inputs are applied first to transfer integrality, then to improve primary depth and derive absolute congruences. Grouped detector products are polynomial reassociations without new domains.

Half-trace guards strengthen the old inverse domain. Soundness restores the field inverse; completeness proves nonzero trace from unequal valuations at a selected split contact prime after excluding finitely many bad reductions of already fixed roots. No claim of all-old-witness equivalence is made.

Detector-pole normalization derives nonzero pole input from the retained rational equations and nonsquareness of two. The coordinate scaling respects the stored factor seventeen and remains invertible when other witnesses vanish.

The single-coefficient anchor uses the exact three-adic leading residue under integral odd formal multiplication and the two-adic coefficient valuation formula. The existing quaternion embedding criterion, including zero, yields equal nonprivate projections with newly chosen private witnesses and the unchanged large subgroup.

The shorter scalar norm tree uses opposite valuation parity to bound leaves. Positive rational norm supplies only one formal place. The scalar point may be near two-torsion; explicit doubling handles both branches before applying the formal logarithm identity. Completeness uses the stronger old preparation and then constructs fresh pole witnesses for the changed input.

The reciprocal scalar chart has positive nonzero d and derives nonzero k by a rational norm obstruction. Exact polynomial identities give the true difference; the extra S=-P branch is interpreted by duplication and excluded by the complete-system anchor. Only then is the old slope inverse restored.
The toric weight circuit solves successive Laurent monomials with e,q and later v explicitly nonzero. The retained square T is not used circularly to define its own source output.
